executiveSummary: GM0047's 2025 identity, generalized boundary, centre, 27,687 residents, 17 neighbourhoods, three BAG places, ten BRT settlements, three rail reference stations and five logical road-border links are internally coherent, and all ten presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Veendam is a peat-colony/canal municipality where induced seismicity, deep salt/gas subsidence, changing water levels, urban drainage and regional canal/pump controls interact. KNMI recorded a reviewed local induced MLn 1.440433 event at 3 km depth on 1 August 2026, but this historical point does not select or calibrate the canonical earthquake: at T+24 the simulator has zero current ground motion/severity yet reports 2,054 affected population-equivalent and exact degradation across eight services without an event ID, ground-motion surface, exposure/fragility, inspection or outage state. Pluvial T+24 emits 0.169841 m and 1,200 affected without rainfall, AHN/soil/peat/saturation, sewer, peilgebied, canal, pump/stuw or subsidence-adjusted drainage state. Hunze en Aa's is actively adapting the water system west of Veendam to salt-mining subsidence using staged 5 cm peil changes, two new pumps, three new weirs, water storage and a larger siphon, but construction/planning is not live readiness. Public registers contain 116 water assets, Enexis/Waterbedrijf Groningen/Ziggo territories, one grid-planning sample, 69 antennas, 18 education locations and no acute hospital, but not connectivity, capacity units, live operation, backup or restoration. The N33's north/south graph links are one non-additive corridor, and Rijkswaterstaat's current Veendam–Noordbroek directional closure through 9 September 2026 is absent from the empty NDW municipality clip; N366/canal bridges, passenger/freight rail and cross-boundary Ommelander hospital access add common-mode dependencies. Current water-board drought/IJsselmeer-supply context and a 48-hour Groningen no-warning record do not calibrate T+72. Exact hazards, service percentages and recovery must be suppressed or labelled synthetic until selected, time-valid scenarios and an auditable first-72-hour action/resource state exist; null, empty, historic, planning and out-of-coverage data remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0047 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, safety-region and statistics inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipal/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs uniquely identify GM0047 as Veendam in Groningen and Veiligheidsregio Groningen, and report 27,687 residents, density 365/km², 24.3% aged 65 or older and 4,618 one-person households. The reference point [6.880728124167982,53.08559237082353] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Seventeen neighbourhoods in three districts sum to 27,695 residents, eight above the municipal control (+0.029%); published households total 12,880 and rounded age-65-plus rows 6,760. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 27,687 without rewriting observations.

Three BAG places are Borgercompagnie, Veendam and Wildervank. Ten BRT labels comprise five buurtschappen, two gehuchten and three woonkernen; different feature semantics are not independent population controls. BAG/PDOK place data use Public Domain Mark 1.0.

District heating and charging are missing in all 17 neighbourhoods and cars per household once; publisher null/suppression remains NoData, not zero. Annual residence omits commuters, patients, school/industrial occupancy and transient N33/N366/rail users.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Current municipal water-overload, climate and environmental planning context
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal pages and 2026 Omgevingsvisie material inspected 3 September 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality says heavy rain can exceed sewer discharge capacity, leave wastewater on streets and, in extreme cases, enter homes; it asks residents to report persistence beyond half a day and recommends backflow valves/disconnection. Guidance is not a current event, sewer capacity model or recession observation.

Municipal climate material promotes wadi/infiltration and retaining rain in soil/open water. The Omgevingsvisie consultation records resident-observed drainage concerns around Sorghvliet and dry-summer soil settlement, but consultation observations are planning/context evidence, not measured hazard surfaces.

Veendam's peat-colony settlement structure follows long canal/ontginnings linten including Wildervank, Ommelanderwijk, Zuidwending and Borgercompagnie; generalized neighbourhood centroids cannot represent drains, culverts, canal banks or subsidence gradients.
Current plans do not establish incident rainfall, free sewer/storage volume, pump/weir state, wastewater quality, road access or completion.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Active water-system adaptation west of Veendam and Veenkoloniën programme
evidenceSources.edition: Project status in execution, inspected 3 September 2026; peil decision adopted 12 February 2025; Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The active programme adapts the water system to Nedmag salt-mining subsidence west of Veendam. Measured subsidence will drive future 5 cm peil steps; the plan adds two pumps, three weirs and storage, removes one weir and replaces a siphon with a larger diameter for both subsidence and peak-rain discharge.

Adopted peil settings distinguish named areas including Sorghvliet/Buitenwoel, Wildervank, Borgercompagnie/Langebosch, Kieldiep and others. Project/decision values are not current water levels, construction completion, connected capacity or event-time control.

The 2022–2027 programme identifies Veenkoloniën veen oxidation, water-system future-proofing, storage and canal/ecology measures. Current authority reporting also says IJsselmeer water is still being supplied during the dry period and precautionary dike inspections are starting; this is timestamped operational context, not automatic heat/drought forcing.
The Veendam wastewater-treatment replacement project planned work from April to end-2025, but the page does not confirm audit-time commissioning or live process capacity/quality.

evidenceSources.publisher: Staatstoezicht op de Mijnen / Provincie Groningen
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Veendam magnesium/rock-salt extraction, subsidence and water-management coupling
evidenceSources.edition: Current regulator page inspected 3 September 2026; 2025 provincial environmental assessment; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: SodM says magnesium-salt extraction occurs at roughly 1,500–1,600 m and the permitted plan runs to 2045, subject to the stated TR-9 suspension/legal context. The regulator describes gradual measured subsidence up to 93 cm at the centre of the subsidence bowl and uncertainty after extraction.

Subsidence effects on water management are mitigated with the water board; attribution is complex because salt/gas extraction, water-level fluctuations and spatial change coexist. The chance of sudden subsidence is described as very limited, not zero, and long-term caverne behaviour remains uncertain.

SodM separately identifies rock-salt caverns around Zuidwending and gradual predicted subsidence. Provincial 2016–2023 material reports up to 5 cm salt-related change near Veendam for that scoped interval; dates, process and footprints must not be conflated.
Subsidence is a slowly changing boundary/context input for drainage, infrastructure and exposure. It is not an earthquake ground-motion record, instantaneous flood depth or current asset failure.

evidenceSources.publisher: Koninklijk Nederlands Meteorologisch Instituut / Veiligheidsregio Groningen
evidenceSources.title: E05 — Reviewed local induced earthquake and current earthquake-response doctrine
evidenceSources.edition: KNMI 365-day FDSN snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026, CC BY 4.0; VRG Incidentbestrijdingsplan Aardbevingen current published reference, blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: KNMI records a manually reviewed induced/triggered event at [6.951,53.117] labelled Veendam on 1 August 2026 22:26:50Z, MLn 1.440433 at 3 km depth. It is a historical source point, not current shaking, a ground-motion surface, building damage, probability or forecast.

VRG treats induced earthquake consequences—such as collapse, leakage and infrastructure effects—as incident processes requiring assessment. A regional response plan defines roles/workflows, not an event-time consequence or resource state.

Magnitude/depth/location cannot be transformed into municipal damage without an authoritative or scientifically governed ground-motion model, building/infrastructure exposure and fragility, uncertainty and inspection/outage evidence.

The local historical event must remain affectsSimulation=false unless explicitly selected as a replay with matching time/footprint/model; its presence does not validate the unrelated canonical preset.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Regional risk, crisis plan, resilience and first-72-hour evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Current crisis plan published reference; updated policy plan 2024–2028; 2026 resilience/budget materials; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The 2024–2028 policy treats sea/inland-water flooding, cloudbursts, drought/heat, wildfire, extreme weather and induced earthquakes as distinct regional mechanisms. Regional plausibility does not select a Veendam event or validate exact output.

The crisis plan defines information, communication, population care, logistics, staffing and transfer to recovery; a continuity plan assumes 72-hour VRG continuity. A 2026 budget document nevertheless says total-blackout continuity is currently not or only very limitedly guaranteed and requires choices/work, so assumption is not verified performance.

Current resilience work targets at least 72-hour organizational continuity and explores coordination/emergency-support points. Household guidance asks for a 72-hour kit, while a 2025 VRG letter identifies short local backup durations for parts of emergency communications. Plans/guidance are not measured readiness or delivered resources.
A June 2026 phase-2 wildfire notice demonstrates drought-dependent regional escalation, not current phase at audit time, local ignition/perimeter, smoke forecast or Veendam impact.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Current N33 restriction and Veendam road/rail dependencies
evidenceSources.edition: RWS notice published 19 August 2026, restriction valid 28 August–9 September 2026; NWB August 2026, ProRail 2025 and GTFS snapshots; NWB/ProRail CC0, publisher GTFS terms vary
supports: Rijkswaterstaat reports active directional N33 works between Veendam and Noordbroek through 9 September 05:00 and diversions via N366/N367/Winschoten. The page's direction/segment wording must be retained and resolved against live road-location references, not paraphrased into a broader closure.
Five logical links use N33 north/south plus N366, N385 and N963. Both N33 edges share one physical corridor and repeated 150-unit ceilings are consecutive/non-additive, not redundant capacity.

The current NDW municipality clip contains zero records despite the authoritative N33 notice, proving bounded empty ingestion is not open-road evidence. Historical bridge closures also show canal-crossing state matters, but are not current restrictions.

ProRail reference geometry lists Veendam, Wildervank and Bareveld; only current service/state can determine passenger/freight use. GTFS 77 stop areas and 2025 freight reporting are schedule/historical context, not current rail, emergency or supply throughput.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public water assets, utilities, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Public snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026 CC0; HWH CC BY-SA 4.0, Mijn Aansluiting Public Domain, DUO CC BY version unspecified; exact NBNL/RDI licences not established
supports: The HWH clip contains 116 realized records: two sewer pumps, five sluices, sixteen surface-water pumps, one wastewater-treatment plant and 92 weirs. One hundred three capacity values are null; thirteen values lack a displayed comparable unit/connectivity in the consumed schema.

A centre-point lookup identifies Enexis electricity/gas, Waterbedrijf Groningen water and Ziggo media, all last-updated 7 September 2025; drainage is empty. Territory identifies responsibility, not network, redundancy, live outage or quality.

One Enexis/Veendam planning sample reports withdrawal/injection nameplate, queues and seven projects from 2026; it is large-user planning, not current load, reserve, switching, outage or restoration. RDI returns 69 antennas and DUO 18 education locations, not coverage/backhaul/power, shelters, opening, occupancy or supplies.

No acute hospital is registered inside GM0047. Ommelander Ziekenhuis Scheemda is nearest at 12.02 km, reporting 24/7 emergency/acute obstetrics, ten rooms and 14,412 visits in 2025; distance/annual role does not establish route time, acceptance, staff, utilities, stock or surge.
